request.spec:
Add a summary panel to the screen. Per grade: the count of people on that grade today (retired
people excluded) and their due-totals added up. Per period: its due-total. Per status: the count
of claims with that status. Every figure must agree with the list.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Add a summary panel to the screen. Per grade: the count of people on that grade today (retired
people excluded) and their due-totals added up. Per period: its due-total. Per status: the count
of claims with that status. Every figure must agree with the list.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the summary panel and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`. The work is front-end only, with no changes to the server or the stored data.

It's a new `app-summary` component in `features/summary/summary.ts`, shown under the sheet totals in `people.ts`. To make sure every figure agrees with the list, it doesn't recalculate anything; it reuses the numbers the list already shows:

- **Per grade (A, B, C):** the number of people who aren't retired and whose grade today is that grade, plus their due-totals added up. A due-total of "n/a" is skipped, the same way the sheet's own due-total skips it.
- **Per period:** the period's due-total, worked out exactly as the periods list does it. I moved that logic into a shared `periodDueTotal` function in `periods.ts`, used by both the periods list and the summary.
- **Per status:** how many of the sheet's claims have each status. Retired people's claims are included here. The test expects this: it counts a retired person's settled and voided claims.

The test also expects a `PENDING` status count. No such status exists in the app, so that row always shows 0. If it's meant to be a real status, adding it would be a separate change.
